summary: "The Fantasy Fan, Volume 2, Number 6, February 1935" by Various is a fan magazine published in February 1935. This issue represents the final edition of the first fan magazine dedicated to weird fiction in America. Edited by seventeen-year-old Charles Hornig, the magazine featured contributions from legendary authors including H.P. Lovecraft, Robert E. Howard, Clark Ashton Smith, and Robert Bloch. Despite its small circulation of never more than 300 copies, it became a premier source for fantasy and horror literature, publishing original works and continuing Lovecraft's influential "Supernatural Horror in Literature."
